template.name: Project: One system for a manufacturing and projects company

div.h1: One system for a manufacturing and projects company

img.alt: One system for a manufacturing and projects company

div.p: ERP, CRM & CMS Implementation
A manufacturing and projects company
Manufacturing
At a glance
The challenge
Sales, purchasing, stock, production, maintenance and billing lived in separate tools, and month-end meant reconciling numbers that didn’t match.
What we built
One Odoo system for sales, purchasing, inventory, manufacturing, maintenance, projects, timesheets and invoicing, with each step feeding the next.
The result
Work is visible across teams, invoices follow completed work, and there are far fewer “which number is correct?” conversations.
Built withOdoo: Sales, Purchase, Inventory, Manufacturing, Maintenance, Project, Timesheets, Invoicing
Project details

A growing company that does three kinds of work for its customers: it manufactures products, maintains equipment and delivers projects. Each has its own rhythm, its own paperwork and its own people, and all three have to end in an accurate invoice.
Like many companies at this stage, it had grown one tool at a time: a sales tracker here, a stock spreadsheet there, and separate ways to log maintenance work and project hours.
Every team had its own version of the truth. When something changed in one place, someone had to remember to update it everywhere else.

ul.li: Sales and operations weren’t connected. A confirmed order didn’t tell purchasing what to buy or production what to build.
Stock and maintenance drifted apart. Parts used on maintenance jobs weren’t always reflected in inventory.
Project effort was estimated, not recorded. Hours lived in separate sheets, so project profitability was a guess.
Month-end was a reconciliation exercise. Numbers had to be matched across tools before invoices and reports could go out.

img.alt: Invoicing became a result of completed work, not a separate exercise.

div.p: We implemented Odoo as the single system for the whole operation, set up around how the company already works, and connected each step to the next so data is entered once.

div.h3: Sales connected to procurement and production
div.p: A confirmed sales order now drives what happens next: what needs to be bought and what needs to be made. Sales can see where an order stands without asking.
Receipts, production and deliveries update stock as they happen, so every team looks at the same quantities.
Manufacturing orders and maintenance work sit in the same system as inventory, so parts and materials used on a job come out of the same stock records.
Project tasks are planned in Odoo and the team logs hours against them, so each project shows the effort that actually went into it, not an estimate.
Delivered goods, completed project work and logged hours flow into invoices. Billing became a result of finished work instead of a separate task at month-end.
There is nothing dramatic about one system, and that is the point. The improvements show up in everyday work:

ul.li: Work is visible across teams. Sales, operations and finance see the same orders, stock and progress.
Fewer gaps and reconciliations. Data is entered once and flows on, so there is less to cross-check.
Real project effort. Timesheets record actual hours, not estimates.
Invoices follow completed work. Billing is no longer a separate exercise.

div.h2: What else Odoo can do for a company like this
div.p: This rollout covered the core of the business. Because Odoo runs dozens of apps on one database, a company like this can keep adding capability without bringing in another disconnected tool. Some of these are Odoo Enterprise apps; we tell you what your edition includes, and what each addition involves, before you commit.
Quality checks at chosen production steps, with pass or fail results recorded against each manufacturing order and alerts when something fails.
Receipts, picking, packing and stock counts done by scanning, which cuts typing errors and speeds up the warehouse.
Maintenance jobs at customer sites scheduled for technicians, with parts, time and the customer’s signature captured on a phone and invoiced from the same record.
Customer issues logged as tickets and linked to the customer’s orders and equipment, with response targets the team can track.
Engineering changes to products and bills of materials, versioned and approved before they reach the shop floor.
Customers check orders, deliveries and invoices online; vendors confirm purchase orders and delivery dates without email back-and-forth.
A website and online store that use the same products, prices and stock as the back office.
Live dashboards for sales, margins, stock value and production, built on the data teams already enter.

template.name: Project: Inali Foundation: CSR campaigns in 2 days, not 7

div.h1: Inali Foundation: CSR campaigns in 2 days, not 7

img.alt: Inali Foundation: CSR campaigns in 2 days, not 7

div.p: Mobile App Development, Workflow Automation
Inali Foundation
Non-profit, healthcare
At a glance
The challenge
Patients, appointments, CSR campaigns, inventory and staff tasks ran on paper and spreadsheets, and campaign reports took days.
What we built
One mobile and web app with role-based dashboards for patients, appointments, campaigns, inventory, vendors and leads.
The result
CSR campaigns are finalized in 2 days instead of 7, and every team works from the same live data.
Built withMobile app · Web app · Role-based access
Project details

Inali Foundation is a non-profit that has provided thousands of accessible prosthetic arms to people across India. Its work is funded through CSR partnerships, so it answers to two groups at once: the patients it fits and supports, and the partners who want to see what their funding achieves.
Doing both well takes close coordination between doctors, CSR managers, inventory staff, supervisors and the people bringing in new leads.
Almost everything ran on paper and spreadsheets. As the foundation grew, manual work started to hold it back:

ul.li: Registration and appointments were manual, which made booking fittings slow and patient history hard to find.
Campaigns, inventory and staff tasks were managed separately, with no single view of what was happening.
Leads weren’t tracked centrally, so follow-ups depended on memory.
Teams communicated through calls and messages, which caused delays and misunderstandings.

div.p: The cost was real. Pulling a campaign report took days, and the foundation nearly lost a major recurring CSR partner because of it. The founder couldn’t see inventory, fitments or campaign status without waiting for someone to compile the data.

img.alt: From spreadsheet chaos to one live view of patients, inventory and campaigns.

div.p: We designed and built the Inali App, one mobile and web platform for the whole operation. Each person sees what their role needs, and every update reaches the people who depend on it.
Registration collects everything the clinical team needs and stores it securely. Each patient’s medical history, fitment procedures and rehabilitation progress are organized on a personal dashboard.
Staff book fittings and follow-ups in a few taps. Patients and staff get reminders and updates automatically, which cuts no-shows and phone calls.
Campaigns are launched, tracked and reported in the app, and partners receive progress updates, so they see the impact of their funding without asking for a report.

CSR managers, lead managers, inventory managers, supervisors and doctors each have their own dashboard and access level. People see what they need, and sensitive data stays with those allowed to see it.
Stock levels update in real time, so components are replenished before they run out. Vendor and CSR partner profiles, including vendor performance, live in the same system.
Daily tasks are assigned and tracked to completion, and leads are managed in a built-in CRM so none fall through the cracks.
The app replaced paperwork with one live view of the foundation’s work:

li.strong: CSR campaigns finalized in 2 days instead of 7.

ul.li: Better coordination. Role-based dashboards keep departments working from the same information.
Transparency for partners and leadership. Real-time updates show inventory, fitments and campaign progress without waiting for a report.
More people served. With less time on admin, the team spends more on its mission.

template.name: Project: Event ticketing with vendor contracts that write themselves

div.h1: Event ticketing with vendor contracts that write themselves

img.alt: Event ticketing with vendor contracts that write themselves

div.p: Custom Web Apps & Portals, Workflow Automation
An event ticketing marketplace
Events and entertainment
At a glance
The challenge
Every new organizer meant collecting details and drafting a contract by hand, and the platform needed full e-commerce to grow.
What we built
Self-service vendor sign-up with contracts generated automatically, plus ticket listings, payments, delivery and behavior analytics.
The result
A marketplace serving 6,000 regular users and a growing number of vendors, with no contract drafting.
Built withMultiple payment gateways · Google Analytics · Microsoft Clarity
Project details

Our client runs an online marketplace where event organizers sell tickets for festivals, raves and parties. Organizers, the platform’s vendors, list their events; fans discover them, buy tickets and receive them online.
A marketplace like this grows on two things: how easily new organizers can join, and how easily fans can buy.
The client needed a platform that could run both sides of the marketplace without a team doing paperwork in between:

ul.li: Vendor onboarding was manual. Each new organizer meant collecting details and drafting a contract by hand.
Selling tickets needed real e-commerce. Listings, ticket inventory, payments and delivery all had to work smoothly.
The team couldn’t see how people used the site, so it was hard to know where buyers dropped off or what to improve next.

img.alt: Every vendor contract is generated the moment registration is complete.

div.p: We designed and built the marketplace end to end, with the vendor side as automated as the buyer side.
Organizers sign up through a guided form that captures everything needed to start selling, so onboarding no longer waits on the client’s team.

As soon as a vendor completes registration, the platform builds their contract from the details they entered and emails it to both the vendor and the client. Everyone has a copy, and nobody drafts it by hand.
Vendors list their events and manage ticket availability themselves, and counts update as tickets sell.
Buyers pay through several payment gateways and receive their tickets online, with a smooth checkout from start to finish.
Google Analytics and Microsoft Clarity show how visitors browse, where they hesitate and where they drop off, so the team improves the platform with data rather than guesses.

ul.li: An organizer registers and receives their contract by email as soon as they finish.
They list an event and set ticket availability.
Fans find the event, pay through their preferred gateway and get their tickets online.
The client follows sales and behavior in analytics and keeps refining the platform.
6,000 regular users buy tickets on the platform.
A growing vendor base, helped by onboarding without paperwork.
No manual contract drafting. Every vendor contract is generated the moment registration is complete.
Decisions based on data, with analytics showing how buyers actually use the site.

template.name: Project: Machine test results captured in real time

div.h1: Machine test results captured in real time

img.alt: Machine test results captured in real time

div.p: Mobile App Development, Workflow Automation, Cloud
An industrial manufacturer
Manufacturing
At a glance
The challenge
Test results were written down by hand: slow, error-prone and hard to analyze.
What we built
An Android app that records results straight from the testing machines, secure central storage and a web platform with dashboards.
The result
No manual entry errors, results available the moment a test finishes, and trends visible on dashboards.
Built withAndroid app · Encrypted data transfer · Web platform with dashboards
Project details

Our client is an industrial manufacturer whose products are tested against strict quality standards. Every test produces results that have to be stored safely and made available to the people responsible for quality and production.
The company manages these results on a dedicated record-keeping platform used across its manufacturing units.
Recording tests by hand doesn’t scale:

ul.li: Manual entry caused errors, and every error in a test record is a quality risk.
Results took time to reach people, because they had to be written up first.
Data was hard to analyze. Spotting a trend or an anomaly meant digging through records.
Access had to be controlled. Different people needed different data sets, and nothing more.

div.p: The client wanted results captured digitally at the machine, stored securely in one place and presented in a way people could actually read.

img.alt: Test data captured at the machine, not copied from a clipboard.

div.p: We built a system that takes test data from the machine to a dashboard without anyone retyping it.
An Android app connects directly to the testing machines and records results in real time, so the number in the system is the number the machine produced.
Captured results travel to a central server over encrypted connections and are stored there, ready for future access and analysis.
Authorized users log in to a web platform to see the data. Access is managed per user, so each person sees only the data sets relevant to them.
Results are turned into graphs and charts that make trends, anomalies and performance easy to see, including for teams monitoring remotely.
Each user arranges a dashboard with the line charts, bar graphs and pie charts that matter to their role.

ul.li: A test runs on the machine.
The Android app records the result and sends it, encrypted, to the central server.
The result appears on the web platform for users with access.
Dashboards update, so managers see trends without compiling anything.
Accurate records. Automated capture removed manual entry errors.
Faster decisions. Results are available as soon as a test finishes, and charts make them easy to interpret.
Less effort for technical staff and managers, who no longer write up or compile results.
Secure, personal access. Each user sees the data they need on their own dashboard.

template.name: Project: MyWanderloop: notifications users actually receive

div.h1: MyWanderloop: notifications users actually receive

img.alt: MyWanderloop: notifications users actually receive

div.p: Workflow Automation, Custom Web Apps & Portals
MyWanderloop
Consumer platform
At a glance
The challenge
The platform depends on real-time SMS and email, and needed fast, high-volume delivery without a complicated setup.
What we built
MSG91 integrated into the back end: automated SMS on DLT-compliant templates, transactional email, webhooks and delivery logs.
The result
Sign-up and security checks run automatically, and every message is delivered quickly and tracked.
Built withMSG91 SMS and email APIs · Webhooks · DLT-compliant templates
Project details

MyWanderloop runs a consumer platform that depends on messages arriving on time. Sign-up verification codes, transactional alerts and account updates reach users by SMS or email, and each one matters at the moment it is sent.
A verification code that arrives late is a user who gives up.
MyWanderloop needed messaging that was fast, reliable and simple to run:

ul.li: High volume without delays. Codes and alerts had to go out immediately, even at busy times.
India’s telecom rules. Transactional SMS in India has to use registered DLT templates to be delivered.
Visibility. The team needed to know a message was delivered, not just sent.
Low operational overhead. The setup couldn’t need constant attention from the team.

img.alt: Every SMS and email tracked from send to delivery.

div.p: We integrated MSG91’s cloud communication APIs into the platform’s back end and automated every message the platform sends.
Verification codes, alerts and updates trigger automatically from events in the platform, using DLT-compliant templates.
Account and transaction emails go out through the same integration, with consistent templates.
Delivery events come back to the platform through webhooks, so the system knows what happened to each message.
Every SMS and email is logged from send to delivery, which makes problems easy to spot and support questions easy to answer.

ul.li: Smoother onboarding. Sign-up verification runs on its own, with codes delivered quickly.
Full delivery visibility, with real-time logs for every message.
Low maintenance, so the team spends its time on the product, not the plumbing.

div.h1: The Arc: rescued mid-build, now 50,000+ monthly visitors

img.alt: The Arc: rescued mid-build, now 50,000+ monthly visitors

div.p: Project Rescue, Custom Web Apps & Portals
The Arc
Media
At a glance
The challenge
The previous vendor abandoned the platform mid-build, leaving editorial, internal and reader-facing features unfinished.
What we built
We finished and refined the platform, moved the reader site to Next.js and built a custom CMS with rich article components.
The result
The Arc now serves 50,000+ visitors a month, with PageSpeed scores ahead of its competitors.
Built withNext.js · Custom CMS
Project details

The Arc is a seed-funded news platform covering India’s high-growth companies, with research-backed reporting for general readers and executives. Its journalists publish news and insights for an audience that follows the startup ecosystem closely.
For a publisher, two things decide success: how easily journalists can publish good work, and how quickly readers and search engines can find it.
The Arc’s previous IT vendor walked away in the middle of development. That left the team with a platform they depended on but couldn’t fully use:

ul.li: Editorial tools were incomplete, which made writing and managing articles harder than it should be.
Internal features were unfinished, including organizational information and daily team operations.
The reader-facing site had to perform. For a news platform, speed and search visibility drive audience growth.

div.p: The Arc needed a partner who could take over someone else’s code, finish it properly and raise the standard.

img.alt: “They quickly understood our vision at The Arc and turned it into practical digital solutions.” Aditi Shrivastava, Co-founder, The Arc

div.p: We started with a thorough audit of what had been built, refined the existing features until they worked as intended, then rebuilt the parts that mattered most for growth.
We moved the reader-facing website to Next.js, which renders pages quickly and is easy for search engines to index. For a news platform, that means more readers finding stories through search.
The editorial team got a content management system built around how they write, with rich formatting such as bold, italics and links, so articles are well structured and easy to read.
Articles can include author insights, company financials and shareholding details, giving readers context alongside the story.
Internal tools to manage organizational information and track the team’s progress, so the newsroom runs from one place.

ul.li: PageSpeed scores ahead of competitors, which helps readers and search rankings alike.

li.strong: A newsroom that publishes without fighting its tools.

ul.li: A platform ready to grow, after starting from an abandoned build.

div.h1: MCCIA: online event payments for Pune’s chamber of commerce

img.alt: MCCIA: online event payments for Pune’s chamber of commerce

div.p: Custom Web Apps & Portals
MCCIA (Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture)
Industry body
At a glance
The challenge
Event registration and payment were manual, causing delays for members and extra work for staff.
What we built
Razorpay integrated into MCCIA’s event system, with a simple booking flow, automatic receipts and real-time booking sync.
The result
More registrations handled without extra admin, instant confirmation for attendees and easier reconciliation.
Built withRazorpay
Project details

The Mahratta Chamber of Commerce, Industries and Agriculture (MCCIA) is Pune’s chamber of commerce, with more than 80 years of history and over 3,000 members across sectors. From the MCCIA Trade Tower in Pune, a team of around 90 professionals works on business associations, advocacy and services for members.
Events are central to that work: industry seminars, workshops, networking sessions and conferences run throughout the year, for members and non-members alike.
As the event calendar grew, the manual booking process couldn’t keep up:

ul.li: Registration and payment happened offline, which meant delays for attendees and follow-ups for staff.

li.strong: Confirmations and receipts were handled by hand.

ul.li: Bookings weren’t synced with event availability, so seats had to be checked manually.

div.p: MCCIA wanted a secure, simple way for anyone to book and pay for an event online.

img.alt: Book, pay and get a receipt in one step.

div.p: We integrated a payment gateway into MCCIA’s existing event platform and automated everything that happens after someone pays.
Attendees pay by credit or debit card, net banking or mobile wallet, whichever they prefer.
Custom registration and confirmation screens take members and non-members from choosing an event to paying in a few steps.
As soon as a payment succeeds, the attendee receives a confirmation email and a receipt, with no staff involvement.

div.h3: Real-time sync with the event system
div.p: Bookings update event availability instantly, so MCCIA always knows how many seats are taken.
Payments run over encrypted connections and follow PCI DSS standards for handling card data.

ul.li: More registrations, no extra admin. Staff no longer process bookings by hand.
Instant confirmation for attendees, which encourages more people to register online.
Easier financial management. Automated payment tracking makes reconciling event revenue simpler.
A better experience for members, who book and pay in one go.

Fashquik hit development hurdles just as it needed to grow:

We rebuilt the local delivery dispatch integration so orders reach delivery reliably, for vendors and customers alike.

Embedded developers only help if they fit the team. Ours adapted to Fashquik’s tools, standards and planning, picked up context quickly and contributed to the existing team rather than working beside it.

div.p: UX & Conversion-Focused Websites
MaxintelB2B
B2B lead generation
At a glance
The challenge
The site had traffic but few leads: confusing navigation, scattered calls to action and a poor mobile experience.
What we built
A research-led redesign: new navigation, a landing page for each audience segment, responsive design and HubSpot lead capture.

Conversions up 15%, high-intent leads up 30%, and far fewer visitors dropping off on mobile.

Project details

MaxintelB2B is a B2B data and lead generation company that helps its clients build their revenue pipeline. Its own website is one of its most important sales tools: if a lead generation company can’t generate leads from its own site, prospects notice.
They came to us to revamp the website so it would engage visitors, capture more leads and convert better.
Traffic wasn’t the problem. Turning it into leads was:

template.name: Project: QR passes that speed up entry

div.h1: QR passes that speed up entry

img.alt: QR passes that speed up entry

div.p: Mobile App Development, Custom Web Apps & Portals
A temple
Religious institution
At a glance
The challenge
Passes were checked by hand at the entrance: slow, error-prone and frustrating at busy events.
What we built
QR passes issued online, scanning at the gate by scanner or phone, and a back end that blocks duplicate entries.
The result
Faster entry, no verification errors and a clear record of passes issued and used.
Built withQR codes · Hardware and mobile scanners
Project details
Our client is a temple that issues passes for visitors to attend its events and ceremonies. On busy days, many visitors arrive in a short window, and every pass has to be checked.
The existing process relied on people checking passes at the gate:

ul.li: Manual verification was slow and prone to errors.
Distributing and checking passes took effort and caused delays.
Visitors waited at exactly the moments the temple wanted entry to feel calm and welcoming.

img.alt: Scan, verify, enter.

div.p: We built a QR pass system that covers the whole journey, from issuing a pass online to checking it at the gate.
Each pass carries a unique QR code with the visitor’s name and age and the event’s date, time and details.
Visitors get their passes through the temple’s website or app, by email or in the app.
Staff scan passes with a hardware scanner or a phone, and the pass details appear instantly, so checking a pass is quick.
The temple tracks every pass issued, checks each scan against the issued passes and blocks duplicate entries.

ul.li: A visitor gets a pass online, by email or in the app.
At the gate, staff scan the QR code.
The system shows the visitor and event details and confirms the pass hasn’t been used.
The visitor walks in, and the entry is recorded.
Faster entry for visitors at events.
No manual verification errors, and no duplicate entries.
Better pass management, with a clear record of passes issued and used.
Less admin for temple staff.

div.p: Secure In-House AI & Data
A job posting platform
HR technology
At a glance
The challenge
Job post quality varied widely, and the platform’s own AI model needed an objective quality signal.
What we built
A scoring system that rates every post on quality, relevance, completeness and industry norms, feeding the AI model and employers’ dashboards.
The result
Better posts, listings improved automatically and jobs that reach more qualified candidates.
Project details

Our client runs a job posting website that connects employers with job seekers. Listing quality matters to both sides: a clear, complete post attracts better candidates, and better listings make the site more useful to job seekers.
The client already used an AI/ML model to enrich job post content, and wanted to give it a better input.
The client needed an objective way to judge job posts:

ul.li: Quality varied widely, from detailed descriptions to a few lines.
The AI model needed a numerical signal to know which posts to improve.
Employers had no feedback on how good their posts were.
Scoring had to fit the existing AI/ML process without disrupting it.

img.alt: A clear score, and a clear way to improve it.

div.p: We designed and implemented a job post scoring system that plugs into the client’s existing website and model.

div.h3: A score built on clear criteria
div.p: Each post is rated on description quality (clarity, detail and completeness), keyword relevance, completeness of information such as responsibilities, qualifications and company details, and alignment with industry norms.
Scores pass straight into the client’s existing model, which uses them to enrich and optimize the post content.
Employers see each post’s score in their dashboard, with recommendations on how to improve it.

ul.li: Better job posts, as employers improve listings against clear criteria.
Content optimized automatically by the AI model, using the scores.
More visible listings that attract a larger pool of qualified candidates.
A more engaging experience for employers, who can see how their posts rate.

Project details
Devdoot was launched in 2021, during the COVID-19 pandemic, by the NGO Sare Jahan Se Acha. Its purpose was simple: connect people who wanted to donate with people who urgently needed help.
Many individuals and families faced shortages of basic necessities, while traditional aid channels were overwhelmed.
During the lockdowns, the gap between donors and recipients grew:

ul.li: Lockdowns and social distancing made it hard for donors and recipients to connect.
Requests needed checking, so donations reached genuine needs.
Offers needed reach, so they found the right people quickly.

img.alt: Verified help, delivered when it mattered most.

div.p: We built Devdoot as a web platform that handles the matching, the checking and the outreach.
Donors offer items such as laptops, mobile phones, stationery or food; recipients describe what they need. Both use short forms with OTP verification.
The NGO’s admin team reviews every submission, and only verified offers and requests appear on the site.
Verified posts are shared on Telegram and Facebook, extending their reach far beyond the website.
Donors and recipients are matched without exposing personal details publicly.

ul.li: A donor or recipient fills in a form on the website.
The admin team verifies the submission.
The verified offer or request is published on the site and shared on Telegram and Facebook.
Donors and recipients connect, and the item reaches the person who needs it.
More than 1,000 people received verified help.
Donations ranged from laptops and phones to paper, pens and food.
A structured, trusted way for people to help their communities during one of the hardest periods in recent memory.

div.p: Devdoot showed how a simple, well-run platform can turn goodwill into help that actually arrives.

Project details

Our client is a law enforcement agency that collects data from electronic devices such as laptops and PCs during field operations. The work has to be quick, consistent and secure, often where specialist equipment isn’t practical.
The agency needed a field tool that met four requirements at once:

ul.li: Portability. Easy to carry and deploy anywhere.
Automation. Runs on its own once connected, without user intervention.
Data security. Captured data must stay confidential and intact.
Compatibility. Works across many devices and operating systems.

img.alt: Plug in, capture, secure.

div.p: We built a bootable mechanism on a pen drive: a customized operating system that does the capture work itself.

div.h3: A bootable OS on a pen drive
div.p: A customized operating system starts from the pen drive and runs automatically when connected, with preconfigured settings and scripts so every capture is done the same way.
Once running, it extracts files, logs and other relevant information from the connected device without manual steps.
Officers view and analyze captured data directly from the pen drive.
Captured data is encrypted and stored to prevent unauthorized access, tampering or accidental deletion.
Designed to work with a wide range of devices and operating systems.

ul.li: Efficient data capture in the field.
Portable, with no bulky equipment to carry.
Secure by design, with encryption keeping data confidential and intact.
Works across devices, so one tool covers different situations.
